SUBJECT:  RECEIVE AND FILE THE MONTHLY INVESTMENT ACTIVITY
  REPORTS FOR JANUARY 2026

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Receive and file the January 2026 monthly investment activity reports for the City
  of Palmdale and Successor Agency.

BACKGROUND

In accordance with Section 16 of the City and Successor Agency Investment Policy, the
City Treasurer is required to prepare and present monthly and quarterly investment
reports to the City Manager/Executive Director and the City Council/Board of Directors.
These reports include detailed information on each investment, including the investment
type, issuer name, purchase date, maturity date, amount invested, and interest rate.
Reporting covers all pooled investments of the City and Successor Agency, as well as
Certificates of Participation, Revenue Bonds, Tax Allocation Bonds, Assessment
Districts, and Community Facilities District accounts managed by external fiscal agents.

The monthly investment reports provide an overview of the City and Successor Agency’s
investment activity and portfolio performance. They summarize total assets, portfolio
allocations, average maturities, yields, and book values. The interest rates presented
reflect the most current rates available as of the report date.

Market values for pooled City and Successor Agency investments are based on closing
prices as of the report date. Pricing information is obtained from reputable sources,
including the Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg Financial Markets, Capital Market Finance
publications, and other reliable market data providers.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Monthly Investment Reports January 2026
March 3, 2026
Page 2

DISCUSSION

Compliance with Investment Policy

As of January, the City’s total investment portfolio was valued at $310,607,794,
reflecting an increase of $6,495,485 from the prior month and a decrease of
$14,081,693 compared to the same period last year. The month-over-month increase is
attributable to interest earnings and new investment purchases.

The Successor Agency’s portfolio had a par value of $17,275,279 as of January,
representing an increase of $7,788,409 from the previous month. This increase is
primarily due to the receipt of Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule (ROPS) funds
from Los Angeles County during the month.

All investments are in full compliance with Section 8 of the City’s Investment Policy. The
portfolios consist of a diversified mix of authorized investment instruments, including
Certificates of Deposit, Corporate Notes, U.S. Treasury Securities, and Government
Agency Securities, each maintained within established portfolio percentage limits.

The Finance Division serves as custodian of the City and Successor Agency investment
portfolios and adheres to the three primary objectives outlined in the Investment Policy:

    Safeguard principal by investing in financial instruments that mitigate the risk of
  market-related losses;

    Maintain sufficient liquidity to meet anticipated cash flow needs; and

    Achieve a competitive market rate of return consistent with policy constraints.

Liquidity

Maintaining adequate liquidity to support operational requirements remains a key priority
of the Finance Division. To support this objective, the City and Successor Agency invest
in two pooled funds: the Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF) and the California Asset
Management Program (CAMP). These funds are designed to support daily operational
needs and provide flexibility during periods of economic uncertainty. Their high liquidity
ensures that both entities can meet ongoing cash flow demands.

At the end of January, the City’s LAIF balance totaled $116,929,296, an increase of
$1,114,167 due to interest earnings for the month. The Successor Agency’s LAIF
balance was $4,027,756, reflecting an increase of $42,142, also attributable to interest
earnings.

The interest rates presented reflect the most current rates available as of the date of this

percent, respectively. At the end of December, the rates were 4.025 percent for LAIF
and 3.95 percent for CAMP. One year ago, LAIF and CAMP rates were 4.366 percent

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Approve Agreement No. A-9738, with Euna Solutions, Inc., for Budget
  Management and Publishing Software for a total not to exceed amount of $263,225
  for a three-year term with an option to extend two one-year terms; and,

  2. Authorize the Interim City Manager or his designee to execute Agreement No. A-
  9738 with Euna Solutions, Inc., including minimal and/or non-substantial
  changes.

BACKGROUND

The City currently utilizes a combination of internal financial systems, spreadsheets, and
manual processes to develop, manage, and publish its annual operating and capital
improvement budgets. While these tools have supported the City’s budgeting efforts,
they require significant staff time for data entry, reconciliation, formatting, and the
preparation of public-facing documents. In addition, the current process limits real-time
collaboration, workflow tracking, and dynamic reporting capabilities.

As part of the City’s ongoing commitment to fiscal transparency, operational efficiency,
and modernization of internal systems, the Finance Division evaluated software
solutions specifically designed for public-sector budget development, management, and
online publishing.

The goal of this effort was to identify a platform that would:

    Streamline budget preparation and departmental submissions;
    Integrate with the City’s existing financial system;
    Improve internal workflow, version control, and reporting;
    Enhance long-term financial planning capabilities; and,
    Provide an interactive, user-friendly online budget document for the public.

DISCUSSION

On November 18, 2025, a Request for Proposal (RFP), was advertised electronically
through PlanetBids to solicit proposals for budget management and publishing software.

On December 18, 2025, the proposal deadline, nine (9) proposals were received and
deemed responsive. An evaluation team, consisting of staff who are subject-matter
experts in budget management and design, reviewed and evaluated all proposals.

Consistent with the Request for Proposals (RFP) procurement process, the evaluation
prioritized the proposer’s technical approach, followed by qualifications and experience,
and the proposed management and staffing plan. While cost was considered as part of
the overall evaluation, it was not the sole determining factor. The table below
summarizes the weighted evaluation criteria used in this process:

Each evaluator scored the proposals independently. The Purchasing division observed
the process, and after consolidating all evaluation results, the firms were ranked as
follows:

The top three-ranked firms were invited to give demonstrations to the evaluation team.
Each firm submitted a pre-recorded video demonstration, allowing the team to
thoroughly review their solutions. After evaluating the demonstrations, staff determined
that Euna Solutions, Inc., best meets the City’s needs.

Euna Solutions demonstrated strong public-sector experience, particularly with
California agencies, and offers a cloud-based platform that integrates budget
development, personnel forecasting, multi-year financial projections, workflow
approvals, and public transparency publishing within a single system. The system is
compatible with the City’s existing financial systems and is designed to improve data
integrity, reduce manual reconciliation, and centralize financial planning.

Key Features of the Agreement include:

    System implementation and configuration;
    Data migration and integration support;
    Staff training;
    Ongoing technical support and software maintenance;
    Annual subscription services; and,
    Integrated budget book publishing tools that allow the City to generate and
  publish interactive, web-based budget documents directly from approved budget
  data.

The budget book publishing capability is a significant enhancement in the City’s current
process. The system allows staff to produce formatted budget documents and public-
facing dashboards directly from the adopted budget within the platform, reducing manual
formatting time, improving accuracy, and enhancing transparency for residents and
stakeholders. It is expected that the implementation will be complete before the Fiscal
Year 2027-28 annual budget process.

A significant part of the CONTRACTORS Budget implementation process is the

Phase 2 – Implementation

Phase 2 consists of several steps that add successive functionality to the
CONTRACTORS Budget. There is some flexibility to how each of these components

1.Component Kick-off
Each component will start with a kick-off meeting, where the implementation plan is
reviewed so that the focus on success and goals is maintained.

2.Overview Sessions
The CONTRACTORS Budget functionality will be presented to the City so that the
Finance Division is familiar with each module, is able to participate in its

The components in the CONTRACTORS Budget will be configured to provide the

The City’s historical data will be imported. The CONTRACTORS have expertise with
uploading historical data from the Citys financial software and can work with the City’s
Finance Department on identifying the data to upload. The purpose of having
historical data includes:

•Many reports require multi-year data for trending
•Historical data is the best and easiest way to verify the system structure
•Historical data can be used to develop next year’s budget and forecasts
•Provides familiar data for training

services.

CONTRACTORS Project Manager will assist and act as a facilitator through this
process.

The CONTRACTORS will deliver comprehensive Train-the-Trainer and End-User

be delivered using web conferencing tools.

 Section 1 – Background and Purpose of the RFP

The City is seeking competitive proposals from experienced and qualified firms to provide and implement
a cloud-based budget document publishing and financial reporting software system. The goal of this
Request for Proposal (RFP) is to improve the efficiency, accuracy, and accessibility of the City’s budgeting,
capital planning, and budget book production processes through automation, integration, and ease of
use.

The desired software solution will:
  • Automate the preparation and publication of the City’s annual Recommended Budget Book, and
  Adopted Budget Book, reducing manual effort and improving accuracy and consistency.
  • Streamline the budget development and publishing process across all City departments and funds,
  allowing multiple users to collaborate in real time while maintaining centralized, consistent data.
  • Integrate seamlessly with the City’s existing financial system (Tyler Munis) and other common
  tools (e.g., Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint) to ensure data integrity and eliminate
  redundant data entry.
  • Enhance team collaboration and communication by providing secure, role-based access for staff,
  managers, and administrators to input, review, and approve budget data.
  • Simplify budget book production, supporting both printed and online interactive versions that are
  professional, user-friendly, and visually consistent.
  • Support additional functionalities, such as personnel budgeting, labor cost modeling, or
  production of a Popular Annual Financial Report (PAFR), should the City choose to use these
  features.
  • Meet established standards for the Government Finance Officers Association (GFOA)
  Distinguished Budget Presentation Award Program and comply with Americans with Disabilities
  Act (ADA) accessibility requirements for all published documents.
  • Improve accessibility and transparency for both internal users and the public by producing clear,
  easy-to-understand budget documents that serve as policy documents, financial plans,
  operational guides, and communication tools.

The software must feature an intuitive, browser-based interface that requires minimal technical expertise,
enabling seamless updates, automated formatting, and consistent presentation without the need for
programming or graphic design experience.

City of Palmdale Background

The City of Palmdale (City) is a charter city incorporated in 1962 that is governed by a five-member council
whose members are elected by district. The City operates under a Council/City Manager form of
government. It has experienced phenomenal growth, from 2.1 square miles with 26,000 residents in 1962
to 104.59 square miles and 167,000 residents today. Palmdale is ideally located in the high desert of the
Antelope Valley in Los Angeles County, 60 miles north of downtown Los Angeles. It is bounded by the City
of Lancaster to the north, Quartz Hill and Leona Valley to the west, Lake Los Angeles and Littlerock to the
east, and Acton to the south.

Palmdale has a desert landscape with a seasonal climate, open space, and plenty of room to breathe fresh
air. The people who live and work in Palmdale find a sense of place; the City has a young population with
residents looking to buy property, raise families, and work near home. Palmdale has some of the most

The City is seeking proposals from experienced and qualified firms to provide and implement a cloud-
based budget document publishing and financial reporting software system. The goal of this Request for

planning, and budget book production processes through automation, integration, and ease of use.

A. Introduction and Objectives
  The City of Palmdale (“the City”) seeks qualified vendors to provide, configure, implement, and
  support a comprehensive, cloud-based budget book publishing and financial reporting software
  system. The system must enable efficient production of the City’s annual Recommended Budget Book,
  and Adopted Budget Book, as well as support long-term budgeting, forecasting, and public
  transparency initiatives. The proposed solution should:

  •  Integrate seamlessly with the City’s existing Tyler Munis ERP system and Microsoft Office
  applications;
  •  Support collaborative, concurrent editing by multiple users with defined role-based security;
  •  Provide automated publishing tools for ADA-compliant, interactive online and print-ready
  documents;
  •  Offer an intuitive, user-friendly interface requiring minimal technical expertise;
  •  Include comprehensive implementation, training, maintenance, and support services.

B. General Requirements
  The Vendor’s software must, at a minimum, provide the following capabilities:
  •  Platform and Accessibility
  o Fully cloud-hosted, web-based solution accessible via modern browsers (Chrome, Edge).
  o Support for multiple concurrent users.
  o Dedicated test and production environments.
  o Compliance with ADA and Section 508 accessibility standards (PDF/Universal Accessibility
  International Standard 14289-1:2014).
  o Public-facing portal for publishing budget information online with City branding (logos, colors,
  styles).

  •  Integration
  o Tyler Munis Integration: Seamless, automated data exchange and synchronization of financial
  data, account structures, and hierarchies.
  o Microsoft Office Integration: Compatibility with Word, Excel, and PowerPoint for data
  import/export.
  o API Support: Ability to integrate with other third-party applications as needed.

  •  Administration
  o Role-based security and access controls with Active Directory or equivalent authentication
  support.
  o Administrative tools to lock and unlock budget phases, user sessions, or sections.
  o Full audit trail capturing edits, comments, and approvals with timestamps.

  •  Security and Compliance Requirements
  o Vendors must address how their proposed solution meets the following security, compliance,
  and data protection standards:
  o Protection of Sensitive Data
  o The software must support methods to protect Criminal Justice Information (CJI), Protected
  Health Information (PHI), Personally Identifiable Information (PII), third-party proprietary
  data, and comply with HIPAA regulations.
  o Please describe how these protections are implemented and maintained within your solution.
  o Ongoing Vendor Support
  o The vendor must provide active, continuous support for all components of the solution.
  o Please confirm your support model and escalation processes.
  o Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

  o Support for operating, capital, and personnel budgeting.

  o Customizable workflow automation for review, scoring, ranking, and approval processes.
  o Forms-based data entry for departmental submissions with attachment and comment

D. Document Production Requirements

  •  Budget Book Production (Recommended and Adopted)
  o The system must enable production of both a Recommended Budget Book and Adopted

  Our consultants will work with your team to ensure viable solutions are considered and noted.

  2. Gap Analysis

  A significant part of the Euna Budget implementation process is the functional analysis step (also
  known as “gap analysis”). Although this begins formally after Euna has been selected, and the
  agreement with the customer has been executed, a good part of the functional analysis takes place
  prior to contract signing.

  This step helps both the City and Euna to understand how the Euna Budget solution can be best
  configured to meet the needs of your organization, thus mitigating project risks that might otherwise
  occur. Together, we evaluate, review, and discuss the City’s current budget processes and data
  requirements, and map these to the Euna Budget functionality.

  3. Workflow

  The workflow plan for the project is a working document that will be presented to the City to ensure that
  there is general agreement on the strategy.

  4. Plan Documentation

  We will create a Project Plan and Timeline, as well as Testing and User Acceptance documents. The
  Euna Project Manager will assemble these documents in a shared document repository.

  5. Plan Approval

  The plan will be submitted to the City for review and comment. Euna and the City will have worked
  together closely to this point, so there should be no last-minute surprises. The expectation is that minor
  changes and refinements may be required at this point. Indeed, such minor changes will likely
  happen throughout the implementation.

  Phase 2 – Implementation
  Phase 2 consists of several steps that add successive functionality to Euna Budget. There is some
  flexibility to how each of these components will be implemented, but we are proposing that the following
  plan be used:

  1. Component Kick-off

  Each component will start with a kick-off meeting, where the implementation plan is reviewed so that
  the focus on success and goals is maintained.

  2. Overview Sessions

  The Euna Budget functionality will be presented to the City so that the Finance Division is familiar with
  each module, is able to participate in its configuration, and understands data import needs.

  3. Configuration

  The components in Euna Budget will be configured to provide the City’s desired functionality and
  accommodate the related data imports.

  4. Data Import

  The City’s historical data will be imported. Our team has expertise with uploading historical data from
  your financial software and can work with the City’s Finance Department on identifying the data to
  upload. The purpose of having historical data includes:

  1. Many reports require multi-year data for trending

  2. Historical data is the best and easiest way to verify the system structure

  3. Historical data can be used to develop next year’s budget and forecasts

  4. Provides familiar data for training

  5. Customizations and Report Development

  Customized functionality, if applicable, and reporting according to the scope of services will be
  introduced and reviewed. This task benefits from the data import, as any screens or reports will reflect
  the actual and familiar data imported.

  Report development will be staged as follows:

  1. Reports required for budget development

  2. Reports required for high-level review and approval

  3. Reports required for on-going budget management

  6. Security Setup

  Creating different security roles and ensuring each user is assigned appropriate role(s). This may
  include disabling some accounts, views, or reports for select users.

  7. Financial and HR System Integration

  Configuring interfaces to the City’s Tyler Munis ERP system according to the scope of services.

  Euna Budget Professional
  Operating Budget Module
  The Operating Budgeting Module forms the cornerstone of Euna Budget Professional, delivering
  comprehensive capabilities to create, manage, and analyze complex operating budgets across diverse
  departments, funds, and organizational hierarchies. This module allows the City to structure its budget
  by multiple dimensions, supporting cross-
  departmental coordination and clear financial
  oversight.

  Budgets can be categorized on an
  organizational basis where cost centers roll-up
  into their respective departments and can also
  be categorized on a Fund basis where cost
  centers roll-up into their particular funds and
  fund categories. Cost centers can easily be
  moved from one department and division to
  another, as well as from one fund to the next.
  Additional hierarchical structures can be
  configured as needed.

  Role-based security ensures that users have streamlined access to only the data and functions that
  they need. Cost Center information can be maintained, and comments, notes, and attachments (e.g.,
  scans, documents, or links) may be added to the budget or even to the detailed line items.

  The Euna Budget Personnel Module delivers highly granular and dynamic workforce budgeting
  functionality, allowing the City to accurately model every aspect of labor costs with precision and
  foresight. This module supports the full spectrum of workforce planning activities, from long-term
  scenario modeling to short-term staffing adjustments.

  The Personnel module is well suited to support the City’s position budget – it is essentially a calculator
  that supports the ability to accurately model and forecast all costs associated with positions (filled and
  vacant) and employees (FT, PT and Temp) to accommodate the workforce budget. Step or pay
  increases, cost of living adjustments, new benefits, etc., can all be efficiently budgeted.

  Each Position is a record of all the information required to calculate the base wage, as well as overhead
  costs such as benefits, allowances, and employer taxes; and each are attributed to the appropriate GL
  Account (object code). Personnel or positions which are paid according to a collective contract are
  assigned a pay grade and step, allowing the pay to be determined from the pay scale for that contract.
  Alternatively, a position’s base wage can be entered as a distinct salary value for each position, or as a
  percentile of the range configured for a selected grade.

  With Euna Budget, the City can budget and forecast by position, employee, or by both – applying fringe
  benefit rates with escalating factors, making salary modifications by employee classifications, and
  more. Positions can include the assigned employee or may represent an unfilled/vacant position.
  System reports display filled and unfilled position counts at each hierarchical level of the organization.

  Key Features:

  •  Detailed salary and benefits calculations at the individual employee and position level,

  •  Integrated support for collective bargaining agreements across multiple unions and bargaining

  Forecasting features
  Euna Budget supports unlimited multi-year planning and forecasting for revenue, expense, and
  positions. Forecasting can be performed within all Euna Budget modules. Processes may include
  projecting year-end values (often based on Budget to Actual analysis) and/or forecasting future years.

  algorithms.

BACKGROUND

The Council Chamber is the City’s main location for City Council meetings, as well as
other public meetings and hearings. Council meetings must be reliably broadcast and
streamed to ensure public access and transparency.

Recent State legislation, Senate Bill 707 (SB 707), expanded requirements for public
meeting access and remote participation. The law strengthens Brown Act requirements
by mandating hybrid participation, high-definition video, real-time streaming, closed
captioning, and ADA-compliant accessibility.

The current Council Chamber broadcast and audiovisual system was installed in 2018. It
now relies on aging equipment, some of which has been discontinued by manufacturers.
Replacement parts and software support are becoming harder to obtain, increasing the
risk of system failures or service interruptions. The system was not designed to fully
support integrated captioning, multi-platform streaming backups, digital signage, or
modern AV-over-IP technology. It also lacks the flexibility, scalability, and redundancy
needed to meet current and future operational and legal requirements.

To meet these legal requirements and reduce compliance risks, the City must maintain a
system that can:

    Provide stable live streaming and recording with backup systems
    Support both in-person and remote public comments
    Include real-time closed captioning and accessibility features
    Deliver high-quality video and clear audio for all participants
    Operate reliably to prevent disruptions that could limit public access

DISCUSSION

The proposed project will upgrade the City Council Chamber’s audio and video system.
This project will replace that equipment with a modern, reliable system that improves
video quality, enhances sound clarity, adds real-time closed captioning, and strengthens
live streaming reliability. These improvements will better support both in-person and
remote participation, ensure accessibility for community members who rely on ADA
accommodations, and help the City continue meeting state public access requirements.

IMS originally designed and installed the existing system and has detailed knowledge of
its construction and programming. This familiarity will allow the upgrade to be completed
more efficiently and with less risk of service interruptions during Council meetings.

The upgraded system will provide better video quality, clearer sound for people in the
room and online, real-time closed captioning, and more reliable streaming with backup
protection. It will also make the system easier for staff to operate. These improvements
will support both in-person and remote public participation, ensure ADA accessibility, and
reduce service interruptions caused by equipment failure. Overall, the project helps the

City continue to meet Brown Act requirements, including the increased public access

Because this project is highly specialized and IMS is already familiar with the current
system, staff used the City’s “Best Interest” purchasing rule under the Palmdale Municipal
Code. This rule allows the City to skip a formal bidding process when it serves the City’s
best interest. Staff determined that using IMS lowers project risk, prevents delays that
could happen if a new vendor had to learn and redesign the system, and ensures a
smooth transition without disrupting public meetings.

For these reasons, staff recommend that the City Council approve the agreement with
Cashel Corporation dba IMS.

Cashel Corporation dba Integrated Media Systems (IMS or AV Consultant/Contractor) is

broadcast equipment and functionality and audiovisual systems infrastructure supporting the

Contract for Services Between the City of Palmdale and Cashel Corporation DBA Integrated
Media Systems for evaluation, modification and upgrade the capabilities of the Council
Chamber Broadcast systems and the supporting audiovisual system infrastructure to ensure

obsolescence and are capable of adaptation to future functionality.

requested by the City to the systems to accommodate and support additional functionality and
communications capabilities. Additionally, we have provided remote system monitoring,
preventive maintenance, phone support and onsite technical support for these systems.

As IMS has demonstrated to the City, we are a proven integration company utilizing the best
design, construction and management techniques and the most highly reliable and serviceable
equipment available. IMS is intimately familiar with every aspect of system design as it applies to
Council Chambers and broadcast application for municipal communications and has a 38+ year

projects.

The IMS personnel to be assigned to perform this project have worked with the City providing
design, engineering, project management, integration and support of the City’s existing
systems since the beginning of our partnership in 2018.

IMS is an authorized dealer or distributor for more than 400 manufacturers of audio, video,
control, networking, lighting and peripheral AV products. We select and utilize only the most
reliable, highest performance and fully supportable products available.

configuration systems with state-of-the-art video-over-IP (VOIP) and NDI network based fully
digital AV distribution and control systems providing the greatest degree of reliability,
performance, flexibility and future-proofing of the facility.

The following information is provided to indicate the scope of work to be provided during the
implementation phase of the project.

SCOPE OF WORK

The AV Consultant/Contractor will de-install existing components in the Council Chamber, control
room and EOC/Training Room which are no longer to be used and will integrate new equipment,
custom components, installation materials provided by the AV Consultant/Contractor and City
Furnished Equipment and cabling (CFE) with those existing devices to remain and be reused to
create complete, turnkey audiovisual systems performing all the services and functions as
described within this specification.

Per the City’s instruction, the previously installed Council Chamber, broadcast and control room
connectivity to the Administration Conference Room, Closed Session Room and Chimbole
Cultural Center is to be abandoned and these areas are no longer to be interfaced to the Council
Chamber, broadcast and control room systems. The EOC/Training Room integration to the
Council Chamber and broadcast systems will remain with equivalent functionality to the existing
system.

The AV Consultant/Contractor will provide the following services to the City, as required.
Specifically, the scope of work will include, but is not limited to:

  •  AV and Broadcast System Detailed Engineering
  •  Provided and CFE Equipment Coordination and Supply
  •  CFE cabling specification and documentation
  •  Project Management
  •  Construction and Systems Coordination
  •  System Production
  •  Control System Modification and Reprogramming
  •  Factory Acceptance Testing

  •  Initial Meeting Support

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Receive the summary of the 2025 Annual Housing Element Progress Report;

  2. Direct staff to make minor revisions to the Report if required by the California
  Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD); and,

  3. Direct staff to file the report with the California Department of HCD.

BACKGROUND

Government Code Section 65400 requires that all California cities provide an Annual
Housing Element Progress Report to the Governor’s Office of Planning and Research
(OPR) and the California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD).
The intent of the statute is to describe the City’s progress in meeting its share of the
Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA). Also, filing the annual report with OPR
and HCD allows the City to continue to be eligible for future housing grants.

DISCUSSION

The City of Palmdale was allocated 6,640 units in the 6th cycle RHNA for the October
2021–October 2029 planning period. These units are distributed by affordability level, and
the Housing Element must identify how the City will accommodate them by designating
sufficient residential land. While the City must ensure adequate zoning capacity, it is not
required to guarantee construction. Progress is reported annually through the Housing
Element Progress Report.

In April 2023, the City adopted Zoning Ordinance Amendment 21-007, updating Title 17
of the Palmdale Municipal Code to be consistent with Palmdale 2045, the City’s adopted
General Plan. This update included additional land use designations that allow flexibility
in multi-family and mixed-use zones to accommodate residential development.

provides a breakdown of housing units per year from 2021 to 2025.

City staff continue to process housing development applications as expeditiously as
possible to support timely project delivery. Staff also meet regularly with external utility
partners to coordinate infrastructure planning and ensure development projects move
through the review process in a streamlined and efficient manner.

The annual RHNA progress report captures housing production for a single year but does
not reflect the City’s full development pipeline. Several approved residential projects are
in post-approval processing and are expected to add units in future reporting cycles.

The City also has multiple approved tentative subdivision maps being marketed to home
builders, representing a substantial inventory of entitled, ready-to-develop lots. Although
not all units appear in this year’s report, this inventory positions the City to continue
making measurable progress toward its RHNA allocation in the coming years.

SUBJECT:  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. CC 2026-013, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE AUTHORIZING THE
  CITY MANAGER’S SIGNATURE AUTHORITY FOR A NOT TO
  EXCEED AMOUNT OF $350,000 PER TRANSACTION FOR THE
  CONTRACTING OF PERFORMERS OR ENTERTAINMENT
  SERVICES AND REPEALING RESOLUTION NO. CC 2025-058

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2026-013, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
  Palmdale authorizing the City Manager's signature authority for a not to exceed
  amount of $350,000 per transaction for the contracting of performers or
  entertainment services and repealing Resolution No. CC 2025-058.

BACKGROUND

Since 1995, the City has hosted summer concerts at Marie Kerr Park, and, with the
construction of the Palmdale Amphitheater, the series was relocated in 2005.
Establishing an appropriate signature authority policy is necessary to ensure the City
can act swiftly and effectively to secure entertainment services in a competitive
marketplace.

In August 2025, the City Council approved Resolution No. CC 2025-058, which allows
the City Manager to approve up to $300,000 per transaction for performers and
entertainment services.

With the growing number of entertainment venues across the region and the state, artist
pricing has become increasingly competitive and volatile. Securing high-caliber
entertainment often requires the ability to respond quickly during active negotiations. The
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Resolution No. CC 2026-013
March 3, 2026
Page 2

$300,000 limit makes it difficult for the City to quickly book higher-cost performers and
respond to changing market conditions and artist availability.

DISCUSSION

The City seeks to broaden entertainment offerings to include live comedy and other high-
demand programming. However, due to rising costs, high demand, and the inability to
extend financial offers promptly, the City risks losing available performance dates to
competing venues and missing opportunities to secure artists already touring within the
region.

Resolution No. CC 2026-013 increases the City Manager’s signature authority for
performers and entertainment services from $300,000 to a not to exceed amount of
$350,000 per transaction. This adjustment establishes a ceiling, not a standard cost, and
does not imply that all performances will approach this amount. Rather, it provides the
necessary flexibility to secure higher-cost acts when warranted, while ensuring no single
transaction exceeds the authorized limit.

FISCAL IMPACT

$0; There is no fiscal impact associated with this action. Funds are budgeted and
available in Contract Services, Concert Program accounts in Fiscal Year 2025-26.

STRATEGIC PLAN

Goal IV: Maintain a desirable community where everyone wants to live, work and play.

  D. Develop and maintain diverse programs and events that inspire growth, pride,
  and lifelong learning.

SUBJECT:  APPROVE AGREEMENT WITH FS CONTRACTORS, INC., FOR
  CONCRETE REMOVAL AND REPLACEMENT SERVICES AT CITY
  PARKS AND FACILITY GROUNDS FOR A TOTAL NOT TO EXCEED
  AMOUNT OF $147,700 FOR A TERM OF ONE YEAR

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Approve Agreement No. A-9701 with FS Contractors, Inc., for concrete removal
  and replacement services at City parks and facility grounds for a total not to exceed
  amount of $147,700, which includes a contract amount of $128,444, plus a 15%
  contingency amount of $19,256, for a term of one year; and,

  2. Authorize the Interim City Manager or his designee to execute Agreement No. A-
  9701 with FS Contractors, Inc., including minimal and/or non-substantial
  changes.

BACKGROUND

In January 2023, the City completed a comprehensive sidewalk inspection survey within
park sites and facility grounds to evaluate existing conditions. The survey documented
the location, type, and severity of sidewalk hazards and identified appropriate corrective
actions. In accordance with sidewalk management best practices, which call for annual
inspections, a subsequent inspection was conducted in April 2024.

Following each inspection, concrete saw-cutting repairs were made to mitigate vertical
displacement hazards that fell below the established replacement threshold of 2.5
inches. For sidewalk segments exceeding this threshold, City staff installed temporary
ramps to address immediate safety concerns until the affected concrete panels could
be fully removed and replaced.

DISCUSSION

The City publicly advertised Invitation for Bid No. 26-001-3500 for Concrete Removal and
Replacement Services via PlanetBids on November 18, 2025. The solicitation was also
posted on the City’s website and published in the Antelope Valley Press. While 26
vendors registered as prospective bidders, the solicitation closed on December 18, 2025,
with three (3) vendors submitting bids:

 Rank  Vendor  Location  Proposal Amount
  1  FS Contractors, Inc.  Irwindale, CA  128,444.00
  2  Airplace Masters Inc.  Victorville, CA  142,640.00
  3  All American Building Services  Santa Clarita, CA  344,700.00

Airplace Masters, Inc., and All American Building Services did not submit all required
documents, rendering their bids non-responsive. FS Contractors, Inc. was the lowest
responsive and responsible bidder.

Under this Agreement, FS Contractors, Inc., will remove and replace approximately
4,828 square feet of concrete panels across 40 sidewalk sections within City parks and
facility grounds. These improvements are necessary to address deferred maintenance
that has resulted in deteriorated concrete panels that pose safety hazards. The work will
improve pedestrian walkway safety, reduce liability exposure, and extend the useful life
of the City’s sidewalk infrastructure. Based on the engineer’s estimate and the contract
award amount, the Community Workforce Agreement was not included per Section
2.2(b).

FISCAL IMPACT

$147,700; Sufficient funds are budgeted and available in Fiscal Year 2025-26. Funds are
budgeted in Measure AV.

STRATEGIC PLAN

Goal III. Invest in infrastructure to improve community livability.

  A. Seek innovative, cost effective, customer focused methods of service delivery.

    EXHIBIT C
  SCOPE OF WORK
Demolition, disposal, subgrade preparation, and installation of new asphalt cement (AC) &
Portland Cement Concrete (PCC) concrete to replace concrete sidewalks, curbs, and asphalt
pavement.

The CONTRACTOR must be capable of performing all related flatwork, including proper grubbing,
grading, forming, finishing, and curing; maintaining safe pedestrian access during construction;
protecting adjacent surfaces and all interfacing infrastructure; exposing tree roots via pneumatic
excavation; and safeguarding uncured concrete from vandalism, defacement, or damage through
completion and acceptance of work.

All work shall comply with current ADA accessibility standards and conform to the latest edition of
the Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction (“Greenbook”), including but not limited
to the following sections: Section 201 (Clearing and Grubbing, Grading), Section 301 (Subgrade
Preparation), Section 302-6 (Portland Cement Concrete Pavement), Section 303 (Concrete
Structures), Section 306 (Concrete Curb, Gutter, Sidewalk, Driveways, Alley Intersections, and
Cross Gutters), and Section 307 (Accessibility Improvements). Work shall also comply with all
applicable City of Palmdale technical provisions (Appendix A – City of Palmdale Concrete
Removal & Replacement Technical Provisions) and standard plans for public works construction
(Appendix C – City of Palmdale Standard Plans for Public Works Construction).

The CONTRACTOR shall coordinate with City staff to schedule work in a manner that minimizes
disruptions to scheduled irrigation cycles, public access, programming, and recreational use of
park grounds and green spaces. Sensitivity to park hours, events, and public safety is required.

General Requirements
1. The selected CONTRACTOR shall furnish all labor, materials, and equipment necessary to
  perform asphalt concrete (AC) and Portland cement concrete (PCC) removal, disposal,
  subgrade preparation, and AC & PCC replacement services for the City of Palmdale, in
  accordance with the terms and conditions outlined herein.

2. Work will occur in high-traffic public areas including parks, facility grounds, trails, active
  recreation spaces and other municipal rights-of-way. The CONTRACTOR shall fence off or
  barricade open work zones to ensure safety of the public, including park patrons, City staff
  and those conducting business at City offices.

3. The CONTRACTOR shall take all necessary precautions to protect existing infrastructure and
  adjacent improvements during construction, including but not limited to existing hardscapes,
  pavement, decomposed granite (DG) trails, turfgrass, trees, irrigation systems, utilities,
  signage, park equipment and site amenities. Temporary protection shall be installed where
  needed. The CONTRACTOR shall coordinate utility marking through USA Dig Alert prior to
  any excavation and maintain an active dig-alert ticket through completion of work as required
  by law.

4. The CONTRACTOR shall maintain a clean and safe work site at all times, including daily
  removal of construction debris, proper storage of materials, and the use of appropriate safety
  barriers, temporary fencing and signage to protect the public as required. Active excavations
  shall not be left exposed after work hours. Upon completion of work, the CONTRACTOR shall
  fully restore all disturbed areas—including landscaping, paving, and site furnishings—to their
  original condition.
 5. The CONTRACTOR shall only use City-approved staging and storage areas for equipment,
  materials, and vehicles. Staging areas shall be kept orderly, secure, and free from hazards.
  The CONTRACTOR shall implement best management practices (BMPs) for pollution
  prevention and containment in accordance with local, state, and federal requirements,
  including stormwater regulations. Concrete washout areas, spill containment, dust control,
  and sediment barriers shall be provided as necessary to prevent pollutants from becoming
  airborne or entering storm drains, landscaped areas, or waterways. The CONTRACTOR shall
  be responsible for all environmental compliance related to staging and construction activities.

Scheduling of Work
1. The City will issue written notice to proceed.

2. The CONTRACTOR shall acknowledge receipt of each work order within 24 hours from the
  date of issuance by the City and shall submit a proposed project schedule within five (5)
  business days of that date.

3. The CONTRACTOR shall commence work no later than fourteen (14) calendar days from the
  date the work order is issued by the City, unless an alternate start date is approved in writing
  by the City.

4. The CONTRACTOR shall coordinate pre-construction meetings, confirm project schedule and
  provide weekly schedule and progress updates, coordinating all work with the designated City
  representative to ensure that project execution is timely and completed in a manner
  satisfactory to the City.

Concrete Removal & Replacement
1. Concrete removal and replacement shall include demolition, disposal, subgrade preparation,
  forming, and installation of new concrete improvements in accordance with City standards,
  technical provisions and the following general guidelines:

  a. The CONTRACTOR shall construct flatwork per City of Palmdale technical provisions
  (Appendix A), standard plans for public works construction (Appendix C) and
  Greenbook (Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction, latest edition).
  Sidewalks, curb ramps, landings and mow curbs shall be 4 inches thick; driveways &
  vehicular access areas shall be 6 inches thick or as directed by the City. Aquatic facility
  deck thickness shall match existing. ADA-compliant pedestrian ramps shall be
  constructed in accordance with current federal and state accessibility standards,
  including detectable warning surfaces, proper slope transitions, and minimum
  clearance widths. Transitions to adjacent surfaces must be smooth and flush, free of
  trip hazards.

  b. The CONTRACTOR shall construct curbs and curb and gutter per City of Palmdale
  technical provisions (Appendix A), standard plans for public works construction
  (Appendix C) and Greenbook (Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction,
  latest edition), with proper flowline grading and transition to existing improvements.

  c. The CONTRACTOR shall construct concrete v-channels, catch basins, surface drains
  and curb drains per City of Palmdale technical provisions (Appendix A), standard plans
  for public works construction (Appendix C), and Greenbook (Standard Specifications
  for Public Works Construction, latest edition), with appropriate slope and cross-section
  to ensure proper drainage and tied into existing drainage systems as required.
   d. The CONTRACTOR shall install reinforcing steel (rebar) per City of Palmdale technical
  provisions (Appendix A), and standard plans for public works construction (Appendix
  C), including proper placement, tying, and clearance, in accordance with the
  Greenbook (Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction, latest edition).

  e. The CONTRACTOR shall match color and finish of any new concrete to existing,
  interfacing concrete in texture, tone, and appearance, unless otherwise directed by
  the City. Where no existing concrete finish is present or where new improvements are
  isolated, a standard light broom finish with natural gray concrete shall be used as the
  default. Appropriate expansion joints, saw cuts, and joint resealing shall be provided
  to control cracking and to maintain visual consistency with surrounding improvements
  per City of Palmdale technical provisions (Appendix A), standard plans for public works
  construction (Appendix C), and Greenbook (Standard Specifications for Public Works
  Construction, latest edition).

  f.  The CONTRACTOR shall coordinate inspections as required by the Parks
  Superintendent or appointed designee.

Tree Protection and Root Pruning
1. The CONTRACTOR shall implement all necessary measures to protect existing trees within
  or adjacent to each work zone in accordance with ANSI A300 (Part 5) – Management of Trees
  on Construction Sites, the ISA Best Management Practices for Managing Trees During
  Construction, and the City of Palmdale’s Tree Protection Requirements (Appendix B - City of
  Palmdale Tree Protection During Construction).

2. When root pruning is required due to site conditions, the CONTRACTOR shall use an air
  spade or air knife to safely expose tree roots, irrigation lines, or other underground
  infrastructure to prevent damage during excavation. Tree root pruning, excavation, trenching,
  or grade modifications shall not occur within Tree Protection Zones (TPZ) without prior written
  approval from a City arborist. CONTRACTOR shall coordinate with the City Arborist to
  schedule inspection and receive written authorization. CONTRACTOR root pruning must be
  performed under the supervision of a City Arborist using clean, sharp tools and approved
  arboricultural methods.

3. Protective fencing shall be installed as required by erecting readily visible 6-foot-high chain
  link fencing at the edge of the Tree Protection Zone (TPZ), as approved by the Parks
  Superintendent or City Arborist.

4. In areas where posts can be driven, galvanized steel posts shall be driven to a depth of 24
  inches, spaced no more than 12 feet on center. The City will coordinate irrigation programming
  to provide for drive-on access into green spaces as needed.

5. In hardscaped areas where posts cannot be driven, fencing shall be supported by wide, stable
  stands, each weighted with a minimum of one (1) full sandbag per stand.

6. Fence panels shall be securely fastened to each other using industry-standard temporary
  fence clamps to ensure stability and security.

7. Fencing shall remain in place and undisturbed for the duration of the work unless otherwise
  authorized. Construction activities such as staging, stockpiling, paving, compaction, or
   equipment parking are strictly prohibited within the TPZ or Critical Root Zone (CRZ) unless
  protective surface and trunk measures, as outlined in Appendix B, are implemented.

Safety
1. The CONTRACTOR shall comply with all applicable local, state, and federal regulations
  throughout the duration of the project, including but not limited to:

  a. Cal/OSHA construction and excavation safety standards.
  b. ADA accessibility requirements for pedestrian pathways and ramps.
  c. City of Palmdale municipal ordinances, codes, technical provisions, standard plans for
  public works construction, and the Greenbook (Standard Specifications for Public
  Works Construction, latest edition).

2. The CONTRACTOR shall maintain a safe, clean, and hazard-free work zone at all times. This
  includes the use of appropriate temporary chain link fencing, barricades, high-visibility,
  reflective signage, cones, and pedestrian detours as necessary to ensure public and worker
  safety.

3. If work occurs adjacent to or within roadways or high-traffic areas, the CONTRACTOR shall
  prepare and submit a traffic control plan to City Traffic Engineer for approval. Certified flaggers
  shall be used where required. The CONTRACTOR is responsible for providing all necessary
  work zone safety delineation at each work site, encompassing the design and implementation
  of all temporary work zone traffic control measures in compliance with the latest edition of the
  California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices.

4. The CONTRACTOR shall be responsible for job site safety and shall promptly address any
  safety concerns or deficiencies identified by the City, including trip hazards, unsecured work
  zones, or improper pedestrian or traffic control.

5. Prior to the start of work, the CONTRACTOR shall submit a site-specific safety plan, which
  may include a job hazard analysis (JHA), emergency contact procedures, and any relevant
  Cal/OSHA documentation. The safety plan shall be reviewed and accepted by the City prior
  to mobilization.

6. The CONTRACTOR shall avoid scheduling work during major park events or peak community
  use hours, unless otherwise coordinated with City staff. Weekend and after-hours work may
  be required in select locations upon City request.

Compliance
1. The City requires full CONTRACTOR compliance with all municipal ordinances, codes,
  technical provisions, standard plans for public works construction, the Greenbook (Standard
  Specifications for Public Works Construction, latest edition) and contract terms and conditions.
  Failure to meet this expectation will result in compliance-based punitive penalties and/or
  liquidated damages.

2. In cases of CONTRACTOR non-compliance, penalties will be levied per incident, calculated
  based on the corresponding line item cost and deducted from the resulting invoice. For the
  first violation, a penalty of 25% will be imposed, escalating to 50% for a second violation, 75%
  for a third violation, 100% for a fourth violation. Subsequent violations beyond the fourth will
  incur liquidated damages.

pneumatic air excavation, temporary traffic control, hazard assessments, and
emergency response.

These contracted services supplement City operations to meet industry-recommended
pruning cycles, address deferred maintenance, and increase service capacity and
operational efficiency, thereby supporting public safety, tree health, and the long-term
sustainability and aesthetic quality of the urban forest.

DISCUSSION

The City publicly advertised Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 26-002-3610 for
Professional Arboricultural Services via PlanetBids on November 4, 2025. The solicitation
was also posted on the City’s website and published in the Antelope Valley Press. While
12 vendors registered as prospective bidders, the solicitation closed on December 11,
2025, with three (3) bidders submitting formal proposals:

 Rank  Vendor  Location
  1  Mariposa Tree Management Inc.  Irwindale, CA
  2  United Pacific Services, Inc.  South Gate, CA
  3  West Coast Arborists, Inc.  Anaheim, CA

These on-call services are requested on an as-needed basis; therefore, the proposal
amount reflects only hourly labor rates, tree service rates, and emergency call-out fees,
and is not a total project cost.

Each prospective proposal demonstrated that the vendor met or exceeded the
qualifications outlined in the RFP, including past performance, experience, technical
approach, and cost. After evaluation, staff determined that splitting the contract equally
among all three vendors would best serve the City’s interests. Awarding multiple contracts
provides greater operational flexibility and will improve scheduling and mobilization
across the City’s urban forestry programs, ensuring annual pruning cycles with industry
standards.

   EXHIBIT C
  SCOPE OF WORK

The following are the general conditions for the work to be performed:

The CONTRACTOR shall have a minimum of 10 years’ experience in the business of providing
professional arboricultural services in support of municipal urban forestry programs.

The CONTRACTOR shall comply with Cal-OSHA and American National Standard, ANSI A-Z133
Safety Standard 2017 or latest edition and all other regulatory safety requirements.

The CONTRACTOR’S account manager and field supervisor shall be certified arborists with the
International Society of Arboriculture. Crew foremen working in a senior tree trimmer capacity
shall be a certified tree worker climber specialist with the International Society of Arboriculture.

The City of Palmdale requires CONTRACTORS to have a trained and skilled workforce, proficient
in current professional arboricultural best practices. CONTRACTORS with tree workers that are
certified by the International Society of Arboriculture as tree worker climber specialists and tree
worker aerial lift specialists will be more competitive.

The CONTRACTOR’S personnel shall wear uniform shirts with the company name and logo
printed or embroidered on them, and they shall wear reflective class III safety vests while working
in city streets and right of ways.

The CONTRACTOR’S aerial lift and other tree service trucks shall be properly equipped with, but
not limited to appropriate safety gear including hard hats, chaps, harnesses, climbing saddles,
lanyards, heavy duty rope, first aid kit, fire extinguisher, blowers, chain saws, sharp chains,
loppers, pole pruners, hand pruners, wedges, woodchipper and hand tools necessary for
equipment field maintenance. All CONTRACTOR equipment must be in excellent working
condition while in service to the City of Palmdale.

The CONTRACTOR shall possess and maintain all required Federal, State and local licenses
and permits including a C-61 Limited Specialty classification license with D-49 Tree Service
subcategory, a C-27 Landscaping Contractor license and a City of Palmdale business license.

It is understood that except as otherwise specifically stated in the contract, the Contractor shall
provide and pay for all materials, labor, tools, equipment, transportation of every nature and all
other services and facilities of every nature whatsoever, necessary to execute, complete and
deliver the Arboricultural services within the specified time. Permits, insurance and licenses
(including City of Palmdale business license) necessary for the execution of the work shall be
secured and paid for by the Contractor.

  TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
The successful respondent shall provide City of Palmdale with Professional Arboricultural
services in support of Urban Forestry programs in Parks and City Facility Grounds, Transit Sites,
General Benefit Landscapes (including landscaped medians), the Fairway Business Park,
Landscape Assessment Districts, Street Right of Ways, and Housing Authority properties.

The successful Respondent shall provide all labor and equipment to effectively accomplish the
following services.
   SECTION A - GENERAL EXPECTATIONS
A.01. The CONTRACTOR shall respond to e-mails or phone calls from superintendents, city
arborists or appointed designees within one (1) business day. Upon receipt of written work
requests from the superintendents, city arborists or appointed designees, the CONTRACTOR
shall create work orders in tree inventory software and confirm work schedule within two (2)
business days. All work requested shall begin within ten (10) business days of work request
unless otherwise authorized by the superintendents, city arborists or appointed designees.

24-hour emergency call outs guarantee a minimum compensation of four (4) hours, require
immediate crew mobilization with requested operations taking place within (4) hours of work
request. CONTRACTOR’S supervisor and/or crew foreman shall meet with superintendents, city
arborists or appointed designees prior to beginning work at each location to confirm the specific
objectives of the City of Palmdale.

A.02. CONTRACTOR’S account manager and field supervisor shall be International Society of
Arboriculture certified arborists responsible to ensure all work is performed in accordance with
OSHA, CAL-OSHA, ANSI Z133 Safety Standard 2017 or latest edition, the Manual on Uniform
Traffic Control Devices, 2023 or latest edition and all other applicable regulatory safety standards.
Tree workers that are certified by International Society of Arboriculture as tree worker climber
specialists and tree worker aerial lift specialists are preferred.

A.03. It shall be the sole responsibility of the CONTRACTOR to perform a Level 1: Limited Visual

International Society of Arboriculture, 2023 or latest edition & ANSI A300 Part 9 Tree Risk

CONTRACTOR shall inspect the canopy, trunk, trunk flare, surface of tree root zone, and site

appointed designees and log findings in tree detail section of city tree inventory.

A.04. CONTRACTOR’S account manager and field supervisor shall be responsible to ensure all
work is performed in accordance with ANSI A300 Standards Part I Pruning 2023 or latest edition
and the arboricultural objectives set forth by the superintendents, city arborists or appointed
designees.

  SECTION B - PRUNING OPERATIONS
B.01. Pruning operations shall adhere to the ANSI A-300 Part I Pruning 2023 or latest edition and
ANSI Z133 Safety Standard 2017 or latest edition. Pruning will generally be maintenance pruning
and shall adhere to the natural pruning techniques. All pruning tools must be sterilized with a
solution of 10% bleach & 90% water or Lysol disinfectant spray prior to pruning each tree. The
City of Palmdale shall submit detailed work requests to the CONTRACTOR outlining location,
service description, tree identification numbers and projected costs. Pruning operations should
remove no more living material than what is necessary to achieve the following pruning objectives,

B.02. Develop Tree Structure improving upon the natural form of each tree, promote or
subordinate certain leaders, branches or stems, head back co-dominant leaders, promote or
discourage growth in a particular direction, promote desirable branch spacing and canopy
structure to reduce the likelihood of branch or whole tree failure.
 B.03. Provide Clearance to mitigate interference with traffic signals and signs, vehicle and
pedestrian traffic and line of sight, streetlights, other trees and public or private property. Trees
shall be pruned to provide a minimum clearance of 17 feet above public right of ways.

B.04. Manage Tree Shape and Size through effective application of branch removal cuts, branch
reduction cuts, and branch heading cuts as required to reduce the likelihood of branch or whole
tree failure and achieve the city’s specific pruning objectives for each tree.

B.05. Improve Tree Integrity by removing dead, crowded and rubbing branches, increasing sun
light and wind penetration while improving upon the natural form of each tree to reduce the
likelihood of branch or whole tree failure. Lion-tailing is unacceptable.

B.06. Protection of Public and Private Property: CONTRACTOR shall be responsible for the
protection of all public and private property and improvements within and adjacent to all work
areas including but not limited to: plant material, lawns, sprinkler systems, drains, fencing, block
walls, brick or masonry work, sidewalks, street paving, street lights, traffic signals, utility pedestals
and all other public or private improvements.

B.07. Restitution for Public or Private Property Damage: Any public or private improvements
damaged by the CONTRACTOR while conducting scheduled work shall be replaced in kind at
the CONTRACTOR’S expense, to the absolute satisfaction of the superintendents, city arborists,
appointed designees and/or private property owner. Replacement shall take place no later than
five (5) working days from the date of damage, unless otherwise authorized.

B.08. Compliance: Superintendents, city arborists or appointed designees shall have the right to
withhold payment and leverage punitive penalties and/or liquidated damages for any work not
complying with I.S.A. Best Management Practices, Tree Pruning, International Society of
Arboriculture 2019 or latest edition ANSI A-300 Part I Pruning 2023 or latest edition, ANSI Z133
Safety Standard 2017 or latest edition, the Manual on Uniform Traffic Devices 2023 or latest
edition, the City of Palmdale’s arboricultural objectives and any other applicable industry
standards and regulatory requirements.

  SECTION C - TREE REMOVAL AND STUMP GRINDING OPERATIONS
C.01. Tree removal operations shall observe ANSI A-300 Part I Pruning 2023 or latest edition,
ANSI Z133 Safety Standard 2017 or latest edition and all other applicable regulatory safety
standards. Tree removals are intended to mitigate hazards and shall include removal of dead or
dying trees, trees with pronounced canopy, trunk, or root system defects, overcrowded trees and
trees whose conflict with public or private infrastructure or interest cannot be otherwise resolved.
The City of Palmdale shall submit detailed work requests to the CONTRACTOR outlining location,
service description, tree identification numbers and projected costs.

C.02. Method: The CONTRACTOR shall consider all tree and site conditions when formulating
each tree removal plan. This includes surrounding obstacles, targets, terrain, wind direction and
magnitude, structure, flaws and lean of each tree. CONTRACTOR must obtain approval from
superintendents, city arborists or appointed designees in advance of any felling operations.

C.03. Protection of Public and Private Property: CONTRACTOR shall be responsible for the
protection of all public and private property and improvements within and adjacent to all work
areas including but not limited to: plant material, lawns, sprinkler systems, drains, fencing, block
 walls, brick or masonry work, sidewalks, street paving, street lights, traffic signals, utility pedestals
and all other public or private improvements.

C.04. Restitution for Public or Private Property Damage: Any public or private improvements
removed or damaged by the CONTRACTOR other than those scheduled for removal shall be
replaced in kind at the CONTRACTOR’S expense to the absolute satisfaction of the
superintendents and/or private property owner. Replacement shall take place no later than five

C.05. Underground Service Alert: The CONTRACTOR is responsible for contacting
Underground Service alert, securing a dig-alert ticket, and allowing the time required by law for
members to respond and mark
their underground infrastructure and verifying positive electronic response prior to conducting any

C.06. Stump Grinding: All tree stumps are to be ground within five (5) working days of the tree

four inches (24”) below grade until anchoring roots are no longer visible, to accommodate the
successful planting of replacement trees. CONTRACTOR shall provide stump grinding work
schedule, and report issues preventing grinding to a minimum depth of 24 inches (24”) to
superintendents, city arborists or appointed designees.

C.07. Wood Grindings: CONTRACTOR shall compact wood grindings flush with adjacent grade

 operations under this agreement shall be reduced, reused, and/or recycled. Reducing shall

 edition, the City of Palmdale’s arboricultural objectives and any other applicable industry

  SECTION F - TREE RISK ASSESSMENT
F.01. It shall be the sole responsibility of the CONTRACTOR to perform a Level 1: Limited Visual
Assessment, as described in the I.S.A. Best Management Practices: Tree Risk Assessment,
International Society of Arboriculture, 2025 latest edition & ANSI A300 Part 9 Tree Risk
Assessment 2023 or latest edition, for each tree serviced during all tree maintenance operations.
CONTRACTOR shall inspect the canopy, trunk, trunk flare, surface of tree root zone, and site
conditions around the trees and immediately report any structural concerns, hazards, pest and/or
disease presence or any other anomaly to superintendents, city arborists or appointed designees
and log findings in tree detail section of city tree inventory software.

F.02. Superintendents, city arborists or appointed designees may request CONTRACTOR to
perform a Level 2: Basic Tree Risk Assessment as described in the I.S.A. Best Management
Practices, Tree Risk Assessment, International Society of Arboriculture 2025 or latest edition &
ANSI A300 Part 9 Tree Risk Assessment 2023 or latest edition. The methodology shall follow
the I.S.A. matrix-based approach set forth in the I.S.A. Tree Risk Assessment Qualification
(TRAQ) program and shall be performed by a TRAQ qualified Arborist. CONTRACTOR shall
utilize and submit a completed I.S.A. Basic Tree Risk Assessment Form or city approved
substitute form (Appendix D or E) for each tree being assessed.

F.03. Superintendents, city arborists or appointed designees may request CONTRACTOR to
perform a Level 3: Advanced Tree Risk Assessment as described in the I.S.A. Best
Management Practices, Tree Risk Assessment, International Society of Arboriculture 2025 or
latest edition & ANSI A300 Part 9 Tree Risk Assessment 2023 or latest edition. Level 3: Advanced
Tree Risk Assessment may be requested in conjunction with or following a Level 2 Basic Tree
Risk Assessment. This assessment may include climbing inspections, detailed target analysis,
detailed site evaluation, health evaluation, storm or wind load analysis, measuring and assessing
lean, examination of the root system using a compressed air tool and/or, ground penetrating
sonar, resistance drilling using a resistograph, and/or sonic tomography of a specific section of a
tree using a Picus tomograph or equivalent, to help determine the presence and level of decay.

The Level 3: Advanced Tree Risk Assessment report shall include name of the TRAQ qualified
tree risk assessor, the date of the assessment, statement of the assignment scope of work,
location, identification, and pictures of the tree assessed, level of inspection and details of the
method, targets, occupancy rates, likelihood of impacting the target, and potential consequences
of failure, site factors considered, documentation of the likelihood of failure, such as a list of tree
conditions, structural defects, and response growth that were observed, risk assessment and
conclusion, options and or recommendations for hazard mitigation, residual risk information,
recommendations for reassessment and limitations of the assessment.

F.04. Compliance: Superintendents, city arborists or appointed designees shall have the right
to withhold payment and leverage punitive penalties and/or liquidated damages for any work not

arboricultural objectives and any other applicable industry standards and regulatory requirements.
   SECTION G – PNEUMATIC AIR EXCAVATION
G.01. Pneumatic air excavation may be required for precision and non-destructive excavation
within the critical root zone (CRZ) of trees or near other sensitive underground infrastructure and
shall adhere to ANSI A300 parts 6, 8, 9 and 10, 2023 or latest edition and ANSI Z133 Safety
Standard. The CONTRACTOR shall utilize a supersonic air knife or approved equivalent and
mobile, diesel-powered air compressor with the specified CFM and PSI rating to power the air
tool, for the non-destructive loosening and removal of soil within the critical root zone for
exploratory trenching, root collar inspections, root zone aeration, vertical & radial mulching.
These services shall include associated cleanup and site restoration.

G.02. Safety Plan: Site specific safety considerations shall be implemented for each excavation
effectively addressing pedestrian traffic control, dust control, noise mitigation, underground
service alert and required PPE for all personnel.

G.03. Site Preparation: Before work begins, the CONTRACTOR shall verify that all utilities have
been marked, install barricades, delineators and caution tape to secure job site, and utilize
protective barriers, such as silt fences or tarps, to protect surrounding areas from excavated soil
and dust.

G.04. Exploratory Trenching: The CONTRACTOR shall utilize the pneumatic air tool to carefully
remove soil in designated locations to expose tree roots and/or locate utilities. The
CONTRACTOR shall excavate to the depth necessary to achieve the city’s specific objectives for
each tree.

G.05. Root Collar Inspection& Root Pruning: The CONTRACTOR shall use the air tool to
gently expose the basal flare and/or anchoring roots of the tree, removing soil to inspect the
exposed root collar for any structural issues, removing girdling roots and other problematic roots
identified during the inspection, making clean, proper cuts with sharp and sterilized hand tools.
Heightened care shall be taken to maintain the structural integrity of each tree, considering the
prevailing winds, and risk mitigation for pedestrians, motorists and adjacent infrastructure.

G.06. Vertical & Radial Mulching: For vertical mulching, the CONTRACTOR shall create a grid
of vertical boreholes within the CRZ, a minimum of 24 inches deep and 24 inches on-center, using
the pneumatic air tool. For radial mulching, the CONTRACTOR shall excavate trenches radiating
out from the trunk, avoiding major structural roots larger than 2 inches in diameter where possible.
The trenches shall begin outside the root flare and extend to or beyond the tree's dripline.
Trenches shall be 6–12 inches wide and 8–12 inches deep arranged in a spoke-and-wheel
pattern, spaced approximately 2–3 feet apart, or as directed by the Superintendents, city arborists
or appointed designees.

The City shall provide amendments for the CONTRACTOR to thoroughly mix with the excavated
native soil or provide imported soil and amendments for CONTRACTOR to backfill the trenches.
The CONTRACTOR shall ensure the mixture is evenly distributed and voids are eliminated
without compacting the soil.

G.08. Site Restoration: The CONTRACTOR shall remove all excess soil, debris, and equipment
from the site, restore the grade to match adjacent areas, leaving no soil piled against the tree
trunk and thoroughly drench all trenches to settle the soil and activate the amendments. Soil
drenching may include incorporation of chelated products provided by the city and incorporated
by the CONTRACTOR to aid in root zone recovery.
 G.09. Compliance: Superintendents, city arborists or appointed designees shall have the right
to withhold payment and leverage punitive penalties and/or liquidated damages for any work not
complying with I.S.A. Best Management Practices, Tree Risk Assessment, International Society
of Arboriculture 2025 or latest edition & ANSI A300 Part 9 Tree Risk Assessment 2023 or latest
edition ANSI A-300 Part I Pruning 2023or latest edition, ANSI Z133 Safety Standard 2017 or latest
edition, the Manual on Uniform Traffic Devices 2023 or latest edition, the City of Palmdale’s
arboricultural objectives and any other applicable industry standards and regulatory requirements.

  SECTION H - TRAFFIC CONTROL OPERATIONS
H.1. Traffic Control: CONTRACTOR shall be responsible for all work zone safety delineation
required at each work site including design and implementation of all temporary work zone traffic
control per the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices, 2023 or latest edition. CONTRACTOR
shall supply all labor and equipment required for proper implementation of temporary work zone
traffic control and shall utilize high visibility arrow/message boards while working on all major
arterial streets.

H.2. Traffic Control Encroachment Permit
Contractor shall submit an application to obtain an Encroachment Permit from the City. Applicant
shall submit, for City review, an engineered traffic control plan when the proposed
construction work involves any of the following conditions: (1) Moving traffic over the
